'''Jabari Ali Parker'''<ref>[http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=22727&SPID=1845&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=209273490&Q_SEASON=2013 Jabari Parker Bio: Duke University]</ref> (born March 15, 1995) is an American [[basketball]] player who recently completed his college career for [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke University]].  Parker was a standout high school athlete, helping his team win four straight state championships for [[Simeon Career Academy]], and was named the National High School Player of the Year by [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade]] and [[McDonald's_All-American_Game#Morgan_Wootten_National_Player_of_the_Year|McDonald's]]. In his freshman year at Duke in 2013-2014, he was named a [[2014 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|Consensus First-Team All-American]], the [[USBWA National Freshman of the Year]], and the runner-up for the [[John R. Wooden Award]] (College Player of the Year). Parker is a member of [[The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints]], a native of [[Chicago, Illinois]], and the son of former [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] player [[Sonny Parker (basketball)|Sonny Parker]].

==Early life==
Parker's family has resided on Chicago's [[South Side (Chicago)|South Side]] since before Jabari was born, and he was raised in the [[South Shore, Chicago|South Shore]] [[Community areas of Chicago|community area]].<ref name=TPYMCANaJ>{{cite web|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2011/12/09/us/the-prayerful-young-man-can-also-nail-a-jumper.html|title=The Prayerful Young Man Can Also Nail a Jumper|accessdate=2011-12-12|date=2011-12-08|work=[[The New York Times]]|author=Strauss, Ben}}</ref> Parker's father, Sonny, has served hundreds of [[Chicago metropolitan area]] children as youth foundation director since 1990. Parker discovered basketball in one of his father's many leagues, although his father has never coached one of his teams.<ref name=CJPbffotc>{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2011/writers/seth_davis/07/18/Jabari.Parker.Peach.Jam/index.html|title=Chicago's Jabari Parker balances faith, fierceness on the court|accessdate=2011-12-12|date=2011-07-18|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|author=Davis, Seth}}</ref> He honed his basketball skills with his brother Christian on the basketball court at his local [[LDS Church]] [[meetinghouse]] in the [[Hyde Park, Chicago|Hyde Park]] community area in order to avoid the hazards of urban playgrounds.<ref name=TBHSBPSLJi>{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1198498/index.htm|title=The Best High School Basketball Player Since LeBron James is...Jabari Parker But There's Somethting More Important To Him Than Instant NBA Stardom: His Faith|accessdate=2012-05-17|date=2012-05-21|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|author=Benedict, Jeff}}</ref> By second grade his basketball skills were superior to the fifth-graders he was playing with and he competed in middle school leagues as a fifth-grader.<ref name=CJPbffotc/> He credits his cousin Jay Parker who grew up with him for pushing him to be better going back to when Jabari was in third grade and Jay was in fifth grade.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2010-12-11/sports/ct-spt-1212-prep-feature-tba-20101211_1_jabari-parker-sonny-parker-youth-foundation-boys-basketball|title=Boys Basketball - Basketball in the family for Parker cousins Jabari, Jay|accessdate=2011-12-13|date=2010-12-11|author=Narang, Bob|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]}}</ref> Sometimes, Jabari and Christian played basketball all through the night at the church.<ref name=BBJAT>{{cite web|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/_UbV0VhdFESDIXEwVkKuCw/boys-basketball-junior-all-american-team.htm|title=Boys Basketball Junior All-American Team: Honors continue to roll in for National Junior of the Year Jabari Parker.| accessdate=2012-04-22|date=2012-04-16|publisher=MaxPreps.com|author=Hickman, Jason}}</ref> Jabari actually made the eighth-grade team as a fourth-grader, but could not play until fifth grade for insurance reasons.<ref name=TPYMCANaJ/> In fifth grade, he had five [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]] scholarship offers as a {{convert|6|ft|m|2|adj=on}} [[guard (basketball)|guard]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-7442451.html|title=A flicker of hope; With Chicago in play for Summer Games, young local athletes dream of chance for hometown glory (subscription required)|accessdate=2011-12-14|date=2007-05-27|publisher=Highbeam.com|work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|author=Modrowski, Roman|page=A80|quote=Parker, the son of former Farragut, Texas A&M and NBA star Sonny Parker, had five Division I scholarship offers when he was in fifth grade. The 6-foot guard, who could enroll at Fenwick, Simeon, Young or St. Joseph, plays year-round, has a personal trainer and competes against high school boys.}}</ref> In sixth grade, when he stood at {{convert|6|ft|2|in|m|2}}, he visited Simeon for a day and scrimmaged with Rose.<ref name=TBHSBPSLJi/> Parker attended Robert A. Black Magnet Elementary and made headlines when he made Simeon Career Academy his high school choice, just like Rose, [[Nick Anderson]], [[Ben Wilson (basketball)|Ben Wilson]], [[Bobby Simmons]] and [[Deon Thomas]] before him.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2009-02-05/news/0902060237_1_western-michigan-simeon-baylor|title=Simeon sweep?|accessdate=2011-12-13|date=2009-02-05|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2010-03-19/news/ct-spt-0320-prep-bkb-state-skrbina-column20100319_1_history-semifinals-robert-smith|title=Boys Basketball - State semifinals commentary: Simeon's Jabari Parker has history, makes history|accessdate=2011-12-13|date=2010-03-19|author=Skrbina, Paul|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]}}</ref> Parker has two older sisters who had attended Simeon.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2013-02-17/sports/ct-spt-0217-prep-bkb-simeon-history-part-3-20130217_1_rose-and-flowers-derrick-rose-coach-hambric|title=Simeon All Access - The 2000s-present: Rose, Parker lift program to new heights|accessdate=2013-02-20|date=2013-02-17|author=Helfgot, Mike|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]}}</ref> However, he has claimed that the reason he chose Simeon was due to his perception of the likelihood that he could achieve team success on the basketball court (as measured in championships).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2013-03-14/sports/ct-spt-0315-prep-bkb-simeon-peoria-manual-20130314_1_simeon-s-jabari-parker-state-championship-kendrick-nunn|title=Simeon All Access - Back and fourth in a row? 2011 Chicago Tribune All-State second team|accessdate=2011-12-13|date=2011-04-02|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike}}</ref> while the ''Chicago Sun-Times'' listed him as a Class 4A All-State first-team selection with [[Ryan Boatright]], Tracy Abrams, David Sobolewski and [[Frank Kaminsky]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://yourseason.suntimes.com/schools/eastaurora/boys_basketball/4433864-393/boat-show-closes-in-east-aurora.html|title=Boat show closes in East Aurora|accessdate=2011-12-14|date=2011-03-18|work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|author=O'Brien, Michael}}</ref> The 12-man Illinois Basketball Coaches Association Class 3A/4A boys' all-state first team included these five and [[Wayne Blackshear]], Johnny Hill, Mike Shaw, Nnanna Egwu, Sam Thompson, [[Anthony Davis (basketball)|Anthony Davis]] and Mycheal Henry.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://yourseason.suntimes.com/sports/boysbasketball/4627007-394/sun-times-preps-notebook.html|title=Sun-Times preps notebook|accessdate=2011-12-14|date=2011-04-01|work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|author=O'Brien, Michael}}</ref> He earned the ''ESPN HS'' 2011 Sophomore of the year.<ref name=JPUSAB/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://rise.espn.go.com/boys-basketball/articles/2011/04/14-class-poys.aspx|title=National Underclass POYS named |accessdate=2011-12-13|date=2010-04-14|publisher=[[ESPN]]|work=[[ESPN HS]]}}</ref> He was a MaxPreps.com first team 2010-11 Boys Basketball Sophomore All-American Team selection.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/_YxfCGxkEeCkhgAcxJSkrA/boys-basketball-sophomore-all-american-team.htm|title=Boys Basketball Sophomore All-American Team: Baltimore sensation repeats as 2013 POY.|accessdate=2012-04-22|date=2011-04-21|author=Hickman, Jason | publisher=[[MaxPreps.com]]}}</ref>

===Junior year===
During his junior year preseason, Parker participated in the July 2011 LeBron James Skill Academy,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dimemag.com/2011/08/chicagos-jabari-parker-shows-lebron-why-hes-no-1/|title=Chicago's Jabari Parker Shows LeBron Why He's No. 1|accessdate=2011-12-12|date=2011-08-04|work=[[Dime Magazine]]|author=Zimmerman, Kevin}}</ref> and he was one of a handful of juniors invited to the August 5–7, 2011 5th annual [[Nike Global Challenge]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.primetimepdx.com/press/NGC11_TopPlayers_080311.pdf|title=Future NBA Stars To Play In 5th Annual Nike Global Challenge|accessdate=2011-12-12|date=2011-08-01|publisher=Prime Time Sports, LLC}}</ref> where he earned tournament MVP honors.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2011-08-08/sports/ct-spt-0809-prep-bkb-scoop-parker-nike_1_simeon-s-jabari-parker-boys-basketball-prep-basketball|title=Boys Basketball - Simeon's Jabari Parker wins MVP at Nike Global Challenge|accessdate=2011-12-13|date=2011-08-08|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Miraski, Benjamin}}</ref>

During the season, Parker established the Simeon single-game scoring record with 40 points in 21 minutes of play to go along with 16 rebounds and 6 blocked shots against [[Perspectives Charter Schools|Perspectives High School]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://insider.espn.go.com/blog/ncbrecruiting/national/post?id=1086&_slug_=jabari-parker-drops-40-in-21-minutes&action=login&appRedirect=http%3a%2f%2finsider.espn.go.com%2fblog%2fncbrecruiting%2fnational%2fpost%3fid%3d1086%26_slug_%3djabari-parker-drops-40-in-21-minutes|title=Jabari Parker drops 40 in 21 minutes|accessdate=2011-12-23|date=2011-12-20|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Rankin, Reggie}}</ref><ref name="Henricksen, Joe">{{cite web|url=http://blogs.suntimes.com/hoopsreport/2011/12/stars_come_out_in_simeon-young.html|title=Stars come out in Simeon-Young battle|accessdate=2011-12-23|date=2011-12-21|work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|author=Henricksen, Joe}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.csnchicago.com/preps/news/Parker-nets-40-in-Simeons-win-over-Persp?blockID=615740|title=Parker nets 40 in Simeon's win over Perspectives|accessdate=2011-12-23|date=2011-12-20|work=[[Comcast SportsNet Chicago]]|author=Travis, Clyde}}</ref> As a junior in high school, he received offers from Duke, Kansas, BYU, Kentucky, UNC and others.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/1187074-jabari-parker-star-must-go-to-college-pass-up-mormon-mission|title=Jabari Parker: Star Must Go to College, Pass Up Mormon Mission|accessdate=2012-06-14|date=2012-05-17|author=Quinn, Sam}}</ref> On February 17, Parker and Simeon won the Public League championship by defeating [[Curie Metropolitan High School]] 53–49.<ref name=BBPLf>{{cite web|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/highschool/ct-spt-0218-prep-bkb-public-league-final-20120217,0,7824890.story|title=Boys Basketball - Following his four consecutive championships with Simeon, Parker (and Chicago's Simeon) were compared to McClain (and Peoria's Manual). Peoria's ''[[Journal Star (Peoria)|Journal Star]]'' emphasized that McClain was 32–0 as a starter in IHSA play because in the 1994–97 time period the IHSA was only divided into two classes. Thus, Manual had to wade through an 8-round tournament instead of the 7-round modern 4-class format.<ref name=V/> However, Simeon won 6 of its 7 games in its final championship by more than 10 points, while Manual only won 3 of its 8 by such a margin.<ref name=V/> In the postgame press conference, Simeon Coach Smith emphasized that his team had to endure the pressure of playing a national schedule that included games against elite teams in distant venues.{{citation needed|date=March 2013}} Note, that with the 4-class system rather than the 2-class system of the past, the 2013 Class 3A IHSA champion was CPL runner-up Morgan Park, who split 2 neutral court 2013 games with Simeon.<ref name=Fs/> As noted above, Rose-era Simeon teams only won 2 championships in the 2-class era.<ref name=JPlteDRs/> Adding Parker's 55-11 start<ref name=JPUSAB/> to a 33–1 junior year<ref name=IBHP/> and a 30–3 senior season<ref name=Bh4f/><ref name=Fs/> gives him a 118–15 legacy compared to Rose's 120–12.<ref name=JPlteDRs/>

Parker is of [[Tongans|Tongan]] and [[African American]] descent. His parents are Folola "Lola" Finau-Parker and Sonny Parker.<ref name=JPUSAB/> His father, [[Sonny Parker (basketball)|Sonny]], a Chicago native, played for the [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M Aggies]] before becoming a [[1976 NBA Draft]] first round selection (17th overall) by the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref name=CJPbffotc/> He played in the NBA for six seasons.<ref name=FkJPg/> Sonny was an NBA teammate of [[Washington Huskies men's basketball]] [[head coach]] [[Lorenzo Romar]].<ref name=CJPbffotc/> In 2013 he developed a kidney disease that requires [[dialysis]], making it difficult for him to attend Jabari's games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2013-03-02/sports/ct-spt-0303-prep-bkb-simeon-jabari-parker-outtakes-20130302_1_jabari-parker-kid-lola-parker|title=Simeon All Access - Outtakes from Jabari Parker interviews|accessdate=2013-03-05|date=2013-03-02|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Kane, Colleen}}</ref> His mother, Lola, a Polynesian native of [[Tonga]], is a member of [[The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints]] (LDS Church) and emigrated to [[Salt Lake City]] at age three.<ref name=CJPbffotc/> Her grandfather was the second Tongan baptized by LDS missionaries.<ref name=TBHSBPSLJi/> Several of Lola's cousins are [[National Football League]] athletes, including [[Harvey Unga]], [[Haloti Ngata]] and [[Tony Moeaki]].<ref name=FkJPg/><ref name=SJPimtjabs>{{cite web|url=http://www.suntimes.com/sports/morrissey/10276613-452/simeons-jabari-parker-is-more-than-just-a-basketball-star.html|title=Simeon’s Jabari Parker is more than just a basketball star|accessdate=2012-01-31|date=2012-01-28|work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|author=Morrissey, Rick}}</ref>  His parents met at a mall when she was a student at [[Brigham Young University]] and he was playing for the Warriors.<ref name=CJPbffotc/><ref name=TPYMCANaJ/><ref name=TBHSBPSLJi/> After helping him find a dress shirt, Sonny left her tickets to his game.<ref name=TBHSBPSLJi/> After he retired and she served her mission, they married and settled in Chicago.<ref name=TBHSBPSLJi/>  The family lives in the [[South Shore, Chicago|South Shore]] [[Community areas of Chicago|community area]] where his parents settled after marrying<ref name=TPYMCANaJ/> and has turned down two movie offers.<ref name=CJPbffotc/>

Parker has six siblings.<ref name=FkJPg/>  His older brothers are named Darryl and Christian, while his older sisters are named Iman and Tilah.<ref name=JPUSAB/> Darryl lettered two years for the [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon Ducks basketball team]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lostlettermen.com/oregon-basketball-pac-10/1995/|title=1995 Oregon Ducks Basketball Roster |accessdate=2011-12-13|publisher=Lost Lettermen LLC.}}</ref> starting for the team in the [[1995 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/boxscore?replayId=1699|title=Texas 90; Oregon 73|accessdate=2011-12-13|date=1995-03-16|publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> Christian played basketball for [[Brigham Young University–Hawaii]].<ref name=TBHSBPSLJi/>

Jabari grew up (and remains) an active member the  Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. While attending Simeon Career Academy, Parker attended [[Seminary (LDS)|LDS Seminary]] two mornings a week, according to [[ESPN]], and three days a week, according to ''The New York Times'', ''Sports Illustrated'' and ''Chicago Sun-Times''.<ref name=CJPbffotc/><ref name=TPYMCANaJ/><ref name=TBHSBPSLJi/><ref name=SJPimtjabs/> At the time of his sixteenth birthday, he became a [[Priest (Latter Day Saints)|LDS priest]] (as is customary in his faith). He has both performed [[Baptism (Latter Day Saints)|baptisms]] and administered the weekly [[Sacrament (LDS Church)|sacrament]].<ref name=TBHSBPSLJi/> In addition, he regularly traveled with his [[Bishop (Latter Day Saints)|bishop]] during his [[Home teaching|monthly visitations]] to comfort the sick, the poor and the elderly.<ref name=TBHSBPSLJi/>

Parker worked out with basketball trainer [[Tim Grover]].<ref name=CJPbffotc/> Jabari prefers individual training sessions with his brother Darryl instead of playing [[pick-up game]]s.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://yourseason.suntimes.com/schools/simeon/boys_basketball/4334020-393/chicagos-next-star.html|title=Chicago's next star?|accessdate=2011-12-13|date=2011-03-23|work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|author=Phillips, Scott}}</ref> Following his sophomore year, [[ESPN]] reported that he had a 3.4 [[grade point average]].<ref name=CJPbffotc/>  By the end of the first semester of his junior year, ''[[The New York Times]]'' reported his GPA was 3.7.<ref name=TPYMCANaJ/> By April of his junior year, his GPA was 3.63, ranking 18th in his class of 377 and his extracurricular activities includes service as the principal-appointed president of student representatives to the local school council, a youth basketball instructor, and a volunteer for [[Operation PUSH]], [[The Salvation Army]] and the New Beginnings Church.<ref name=JPwpoy/> In high school, he was known for carrying a [[backpack]] filled with basketball equipment, along with an [[iPod]], and a copy of the ''[[Book of Mormon]]''.<ref name=TBHSBPSLJi/>
